t: The colony existed for the fur trade: the Dutch depended on Native nations to capture, skin and deliver beaver pelts, and after the Mohawks conquered the Mahicans in 1628 they held a near-monopoly of that trade.
Peter Minuit acquired Manhattan from unnamed Native people on 24 May 1626 for goods worth 60 guilders, a figure a historian turned into the famous $24 in 1846 by a faulty conversion.

Its 1664 Articles of Capitulation kept the liberty of conscience New Netherlanders already enjoyed, and the Flushing Remonstrance of 1657 is counted a precursor of the religious-freedom clause in the United States Bill of Rights.
dyk: New Amsterdam's wal, the rampart that gave Wall Street its name, was built out of fear of an English invasion; when four English frigates finally came in 1664 the town surrendered without resistance.
ev: Henry Hudson, hired by the Dutch East India Company, sails the Halve Maen into Upper New York Bay and up the river that bears his name as far as the site of Troy.
On 17 March the States General grants an exclusive trade patent between the 40th and 45th parallels; traders of the New Netherland Company build Fort Nassau near Albany.
On 3 June the Dutch Republic charters the Dutch West India Company with exclusive rights in West Africa and the Americas.
New Netherland becomes a province; 30 families land at Fort Orange and Noten Eylant from the ship Nieu Nederlandt under Cornelius Jacobsen May, the first director.
On 24 May Peter Minuit and Walloon colonists acquire Manhattan for goods worth 60 guilders and build Fort Amsterdam at its southern tip.
The Charter of Freedoms and Exemptions creates the patroonships; Rensselaerswyck becomes the only truly successful one.
Director-general Peter Stuyvesant conquers New Sweden on the Delaware; Jews are granted full residency in New Amsterdam.
On 27 August four English frigates under Richard Nicolls demand the surrender of New Amsterdam, which falls without resistance.

f.capital: New Amsterdam, on Manhattan (Fort Amsterdam, from 1626; the seat had first been meant for the South River)
f.founder: The New Netherland Company's traders under the States General's patent of 1614; the Dutch West India Company (chartered 1621), whose first director was Cornelius Jacobsen May
f.predecessor: The lands of the Lenape, Mahicans and Mohawks, visited by Henry Hudson for the Dutch East India Company in 1609
f.successor: The English Province of New York, after the surrender of New Amsterdam to Richard Nicolls on 27 August 1664, confirmed by the Treaty of Breda (1667)
